name: Battle of Adrianople
intro: Near Adrianople (Edirne) in Thrace, on a hot day in August. You are the emperor Valens, with an army of perhaps 15,000 to 30,000. The Goths under Fritigern have settled inside the empire and risen in revolt; their cavalry, under Alatheus and Saphrax, is away foraging. Your nephew Gratian is bringing the Western army to help.
debrief: In reality, Valens did not wait for Gratian, though some of his officers urged it. His scouts reported about 10,000 Goths, missing the cavalry that was away foraging. The army marched about eight miles in the heat and reached the Gothic wagon circle around noon, tired and short of water. Fritigern opened negotiations and set the fields alight, buying time. Bacurius’s guards attacked without orders and were driven back, and the Roman left reached the wagons too late. Then the Greuthungi and Alan cavalry returned and struck; the Roman infantry was pressed together until it could not fight, and the Batavian reserve fled. Valens was killed and his body never found; perhaps two-thirds of the army died, including 35 tribunes. Waiting, scouting and attacking at once are what-ifs.

win: The Gothic horse is met and held.
lose: The Gothic cavalry strikes like a thunderbolt.

decisions.title: Wait for Gratian?
decisions.text: You are the emperor Valens. The Goths under Fritigern are near Adrianople. Your nephew Gratian, emperor of the West, is coming with his army and writes asking you to wait. Your officers are divided.

hint.text: Victor, your master of cavalry, urges you to wait. Others say the glory should be yours alone.

scout.text: Two armies together would outnumber the Goths heavily. A few days’ wait costs only pride.

choices.label: Attack now, and keep the glory for the East

fx.text: You will not share the victory. The army prepares to march.
You wait. Gratian’s army joins you, and the Goths face both emperors together.

choices.label: March out and fortify a camp near the Goths

fx.text: You are close to the Goths, behind a rampart.

decisions.title: Only ten thousand Goths?
decisions.text: Your scouts report about 10,000 Goths. It seems an easy fight.

hint.text: The scouts did not see any Gothic cavalry.

scout.text: Where is their cavalry? The Greuthungi and Alans may be out foraging. More scouting would find them.

choices.label: Trust the report and march at dawn

fx.text: The army marches eight miles over rough ground in the August heat, with no food and little water.

choices.label: Send cavalry patrols to find their horse first

fx.text: Your patrols find the Greuthungi and Alan cavalry foraging some distance away. Now you know where they are.

choices.label: March, but in the cool of evening, to spare the men the heat

fx.text: The march is easier, but slow.

decisions.title: The wagon circle
decisions.text: At noon your army reaches the Gothic wagon circle. Fritigern sends envoys to talk, and his men set the fields alight. Smoke drifts over your hot, thirsty soldiers.

hint.text: The talks are dragging on. Fritigern’s cavalry is still away.

scout.text: Fritigern is buying time for his cavalry to return. Every hour of talk helps him. Strike now, before it arrives.

choices.label: Talk while the army stands in the heat

fx.text: Hostages are discussed for hours. Your men stand in the sun and the smoke, without water.

choices.label: Break off the talks and attack the wagons

fx.text: You attack before the Gothic cavalry is back. The wagon circle is hard to break, but the Goths are alone.

choices.label: Pull back to water and camp

fx.text: Your men drink, but the Goths gain time.

decisions.title: Bacurius goes in
decisions.text: Without orders, Bacurius leads the shield-bearers and archers of the guard against the wagons. They are thrown back. The rest of the army is not ready.

hint.text: The Roman left has not yet reached its position.

scout.text: Recall the guards and form the whole line properly, or support them with the whole line at once. A piecemeal attack is the worst of all.

choices.label: Let the fighting spread as it will; the guard has started it

fx.text: The battle starts piecemeal. Your left wing arrives late at the wagons.

choices.label: Send the whole line in at once to support them

fx.text: The whole army goes forward together, its flanks watched by cavalry that knows where the Gothic horse is.

decisions.title: The cavalry returns
decisions.text: The Greuthungi and Alan cavalry come back from foraging and strike your left like a thunderbolt. Your infantry is being pressed together.

hint.text: The Batavian reserve is behind you.

scout.text: Bring up the reserve, pull the infantry back to form a line on the hill, and keep the men from being crushed together.

choices.label: Stand where you are and fight it out

fx.text: The Gothic horse rides round your left. Your infantry is crushed together so tightly that men cannot raise their arms. The Batavian reserve has fled. Valens is killed, and two-thirds of the army dies with him.

choices.label: Send in the Batavians and re-form on the hill

fx.text: Your cavalry, ready for them, meets the Gothic horse. The Batavians come up, and the infantry forms a line on the hill with room to fight.

choices.label: Retreat to Adrianople while the infantry still holds together
